The report now flags an item as `REORDER` when what's on hand won't cover the sales expected during the 6 days an order takes to arrive. I ran it against your `inventory.csv`:

```
SKU      ITEM                       ON HAND  STATUS
CF-1K    House blend 1kg                  9  REORDER
CF-250   Colombia beans 250g             42  ok
FL-100   Paper filters x100               0  OUT
MG-12    Enamel mug                      18  ok
OT-1L    Oat milk 1L                     30  REORDER
TE-50    Breakfast tea x50               25  ok
```

House blend has 9 on hand against about 14 expected to sell in 6 days, and oat milk has 30 against 45, so both are flagged.

- **Changing suppliers:** `LEAD_TIME_DAYS = 6` is near the top of `stock_report.py`, just under the imports.
- **Empty shelves:** these still show `OUT` rather than `REORDER`, so you can tell the two apart.
- **Exact matches:** an item with exactly enough to last the 6 days is not flagged — it would run out just as the new boxes arrive. If you'd rather have a cushion, the simplest way is to set the number a day or two higher than the real delivery time.
